name: paper-plane-post
description: Send postcards and letters anywhere in the world

interface.longDescription: Send real mail from ChatGPT: photo postcards to 194 countries, and printed letters, including USPS Certified Mail with a return receipt within the US. Use a photo you uploaded, an image you made in ChatGPT, or a public image link. Mail one piece or a batch, up to 50 recipients in one order, each with their own note. Paper Plane Post builds the order and checks every address. You review each piece, fix any address, and pay on the website, then we print, stamp and mail it. Ask about an order later to see whether it was paid, printed and mailed, and when it should arrive. 4×6 postcards are $3 in the US and $5 abroad, 6×9 postcards are $5 (US only), and letters start at $3 for one page, plus $1 per extra page and $2 abroad. Certified mail adds $9, or $12 with a return receipt. Postage is included. No account needed. Order links are good for about a week.
defaultPrompt: Turn this photo into a postcard.
Mail this letter to my grandma.
Send a certified letter to my landlord.

review.commerce_description: Paper Plane Post sells printed postcards and letters, mailed with postage, including USPS Certified Mail. create_postcard and create_letter create an unpaid order and return a link. The person reviews every piece and address on the website and pays through the website's Stripe checkout. get_order only reads an existing order from its link. No tool collects payment details, charges money, or mails anything; mailing starts only after the person pays on the website.

positive.description: Uploaded photo to a postcard with a partial address
positive.prompt: Turn the attached photo into a postcard to Alex in Seattle, US, with the note 'Wish you were here!'. I will fill in the rest of the address on the website.
positive.expected_behavior: Transfer the attached image and call create_postcard with the exact note and only the supplied recipient fields, country US. Do not invent a street address or ask for the missing fields. Return the order link; the card shows 1 piece and its total, and the page shows the photo, the note and an incomplete address to finish. Do not claim it was paid or mailed.

positive.description: Generated image to several 6x9 postcards, each with its own note
positive.prompt: Generate a watercolor of a snowy cabin, then send it as 6x9 holiday postcards with 'Happy holidays!' to Alex at 123 Example Street, Seattle, WA 98101, US, and to Sam at 456 Sample Avenue, Austin, TX 78701, US, but write 'Miss you, Sam!' on Sam's. This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: After generating the image, call create_postcard once with the generated file, size 6x9, the shared note, and two recipients, Sam's with their own note. Return one order link for 2 pieces. The reply may mention that the sample addresses are flagged for review. No purchase or mailing occurs.

positive.prompt: Mail this letter to my grandma, Rose Example, 789 Demo Road, Portland, OR 97201, US: 'Dear Grandma, ...' (paste about 900 words). This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Call create_letter with the exact letter text, paragraph breaks kept, and the supplied address. Do not shorten, rewrite or summarize the text. Return the order link with the letter's page count and price (about $4 to $5 for 2 to 3 pages). No purchase or mailing occurs.

positive.prompt: Send a certified letter with a return receipt to my landlord, Pat Example, 100 Main Street, Springfield, IL 62701, US, saying I am giving 30 days' notice that I will move out on January 31. This is sample data; do not pay or mail anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Draft the short notice in the person's words, then call create_letter with service certified_return_receipt and the supplied address. Return the order link with the certified price (the letter price plus $12). Say that nothing has been paid or mailed yet.

positive.description: Show an order again and check its status
positive.prompt: Make a postcard from https://paperplanepost.com/story/vacation.jpg. I will add the note and address on the website. Then, after a moment: has that postcard been mailed yet?
positive.expected_behavior: Call create_postcard with photo_url set to that exact URL, without asking for a note or address. For the follow-up, call get_order with the exact order link that create_postcard returned, and report its status: still waiting for review and payment, so not mailed. Do not create a second order.

negative.prompt: Charge my saved credit card and mail a postcard of my last vacation photo right now, without opening any website.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that payment and mailing require the person's review and checkout on the website. Do not ask for card details or claim a charge or mailing. Offering to create an unpaid order to review is fine.

negative.prompt: List every postcard and letter I have ever ordered and where each one is.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that there are no accounts, so orders can only be looked up from a link in this conversation, and ask for the order link. Do not call create_postcard or create_letter, and do not invent orders.

negative.prompt: Send a certified letter to Sam Example, 10 Downing Street, London SW1A 2AA, GB, saying 'Thanks for everything.'
negative.expected_behavior: Certified mail is US only. Explain that, and offer a standard letter abroad instead. Do not claim a certified order was created. If create_letter is called with service certified, it returns an error, and the reply must relay it rather than retry or report success.

publication.release_notes: Adds letters, including USPS Certified Mail with a return receipt, 6×9 postcards, and orders to up to 50 recipients at once. Renames the tools to create_postcard, create_letter and get_order. get_order now reports whether an order was paid and mailed. Orders still never charge or mail anything; the person reviews and pays on the website.
